title: The Testing Methods Signature Database — Overview: the Signature testing doctrine
body: Signature edition. Original Signature-developed content; never mixed with public records. The Signature testing doctrine holds that every system deserves proof, not promises. Where public practice tests after building, the Signature doctrine plans the proof alongside the design: each requirement is born with its test, each test is born with its expected evidence, and nothing is called finished until the evidence exists. Signature records are original developments of the Signature system — new methods, new framework sketches, new verification philosophies — labeled honestly as original work, built to be executed for real.
capabilities: Doctrine: proof planned alongside design, not after
Evidence-first finishing: done means proven
Original Signature methods, honestly labeled as original
Execution standard: every doctrine ships a runnable demonstration

title: The Testing Methods Signature Database — Signature unit doctrine: isolate and prove
body: Signature edition. Original Signature-developed content; never mixed with public records. The Signature unit doctrine isolates each unit behind a contract wall: the test names the contract first, in plain sentences, and only then writes code. Every Signature unit test carries three labeled parts — the promise, the provocation, and the proof — so a stranger can read the test and know exactly what the unit guarantees. Flaky tests are treated as defects in the test, never tolerated, and a test that cannot fail for a real reason is deleted as decoration.
capabilities: Promise-provocation-proof test anatomy
Contract-first test naming in plain sentences
Zero-flake rule: flaky tests are defects
Decoration rule: tests that cannot fail are removed

demo.title: Promise-provocation-proof runner
demo.code: function unit(promise,fn,want){const got=fn();const pass=got===want;return {promise,pass};}const r=[unit('doubles 4 to 8',()=>4*2,8),unit('zero stays zero',()=>0*2,0)];const pass=r.filter(x=>x.pass).length;J({ran:r.length,passed:pass});assert(pass===2,'sigunit');

title: The Testing Methods Signature Database — Signature integration doctrine: wire and witness
body: Signature edition. Original Signature-developed content; never mixed with public records. The Signature integration doctrine wires modules together in front of witnesses: every interface gets a witness test that records what crossed the boundary — the exact payload, the exact order, the exact timing. When an integration fails, the witness log names the liar: which module broke its promise. Signature integration suites run the same scenarios against real collaborators and against doubles, and any difference between the two runs is filed as a finding, because a double that disagrees with reality is a lie.
capabilities: Witness tests: recording what crosses each boundary
Naming the liar: failed integrations point at the promise-breaker
Real-vs-double parity runs with difference findings

title: The Testing Methods Signature Database — Signature planning doctrine: the proof plan
body: Signature edition. Original Signature-developed content; never mixed with public records. The Signature proof plan is a test plan rewritten around evidence: for each requirement it names the evidence that would prove it, the instrument that captures the evidence, and the threshold that counts as passing. Entry requires a frozen requirement; exit requires every evidence slot filled and every threshold met. Risks are ranked by blast radius — what breaks, who it hurts, how far the damage spreads — and the plan spends proof effort in that order.
capabilities: Evidence slots: what proves each requirement, and how
Blast-radius risk ranking for proof effort
Frozen-requirement entry rule
Threshold-based exit: every slot filled, every bar met

title: The Testing Methods Signature Database — Signature case-design doctrine: hunt the edges
body: Signature edition. Original Signature-developed content; never mixed with public records. The Signature case-design doctrine hunts edges first: boundaries, empty inputs, maximum inputs, type confusions, and time edges like midnight and leap days. Each requirement yields an edge map — every place the behavior could change — and the suite must touch every edge on the map. Equivalence classes are drawn from the code's actual branches, not from guesses, and the doctrine demands at least one case per branch plus one case per edge.
capabilities: Edge maps: every place behavior could change
Branch-derived equivalence classes
Time edges: midnight, leap days, DST changes
Empty, full, and confused-type inputs

title: The Testing Methods Signature Database — Signature automation doctrine: robots with judgment
body: Signature edition. Original Signature-developed content; never mixed with public records. The Signature automation doctrine gives robots the boring work and keeps judgment for humans: machines run the thousand known checks every hour; humans explore the unknown unknowns. Every automated check carries its reason in a comment a newcomer can understand, and checks without reasons are deleted. The suite measures its own health — runtime, flake rate, coverage trend — and the doctrine requires the trend lines to improve or the suite to shrink.
capabilities: Boring-work automation, judgment-work exploration
Reason comments on every automated check
Suite health metrics: runtime, flake rate, coverage trend
Shrink-or-improve rule for suite health

title: The Testing Methods Signature Database — Signature hardware doctrine: shake the truth out
body: Signature edition. Original Signature-developed content; never mixed with public records. The Signature hardware doctrine shakes the truth out of physical things: every board gets probed, every joint gets stressed, every unit gets baked and frozen before it ships. The doctrine's rule is simple — the factory must see the failure first. Test fixtures are designed alongside the circuit, not after, so every net the designer cares about has a probe point. Findings feed back into the design the same day; a test that finds nothing for a month is redesigned, because quiet tests are blind tests.
capabilities: Fixture-alongside-circuit design rule
Factory-sees-it-first failure rule
Probe points for every cared-about net
Same-day feedback from findings to design

title: The Testing Methods Signature Database — Signature verification doctrine: prove it twice
body: Signature edition. Original Signature-developed content; never mixed with public records. The Signature verification doctrine proves everything twice, by two different means: a test proves the code runs right, and a review proves the test is honest. Traceability runs both directions — requirement to test, and test back to requirement — and orphans on either side are findings. The doctrine's final gate is the stranger test: documentation must let a competent stranger operate the system without asking the builders anything.
capabilities: Two-means proof: test plus honest review
Bidirectional traceability with orphan findings
The stranger test for documentation
Independent eyes on safety-critical proof
